messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity and the coefficient of viscous damping. Damping is proportional to the speed of the oscillating body. Body motion through a fluid medium generates a resistive force opposing the direction of movement. Movement at low speeds ensures that the linear viscous model remains valid for the physical pendulum. Pendulum experiments conducted in air require this term when the oscillation period is long enough for the velocity to be small. Small velocities in a gaseous medium justify using a first-order term rather than a quadratic drag law. Law of linear resistance is incorporated into the pendulum equation of motion as a term proportional to angular velocity.

- The coefficient of viscous friction (b or c)

- The damping is small (linear damping)
- When the pendulum is moving through a fluid (air, water)
- When the speed is low enough that drag is proportional to velocity (not velocity squared)
